handoff: Review #2: F1-F14 resolved. 1 blocking — F15 endedWith sets Norn-Outcome on same-step advances (implement.unstick → implement in golden), so a resumed step shows as last boundary (B18/B19). Minor: F16 CI read failure fails whole sync; F17 cat-file --batch missing reply misparsed. Nit F18. human.test flake confirmed 3/3 isolated.

findings.title: Norn-Outcome is set on a same-step advance (unstick), so a resumed step reads as ended (B18, B19)
findings.detail:
`endedWith = (res) => res.advance?.outcome` returns an outcome for every advance. That includes the synthetic ones in packages/core/src/apply.ts: `unstick` (:305), `update` (:321) and `workflow` (:186). Its doc comment says 'when its outcome moved the cursor to another step', but nothing checks `from !== to`. Evidence: golden run-rerun-cancel-2664e609fec7.json and run-rerun-cancel-8d9037dd32ca.json now record the commit 'norn: gh-5 implement.unstick → implement' with `Norn-Outcome: unstick`. lastBoundary (packages/store/src/elsewhere.ts) takes the newest such commit, so a non-holder sees 'last boundary: implement' while implement is running again. B18: 'the last step from the last boundary commit'. B19: 'so that I am not shown a guess'. The coordinator's check that non-boundary commits never carry the trailer fails on this path.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Set the outcome only when `res.advance.to !== res.advance.from`, or exclude the synthetic outcomes that resume a step. Add a decide unit test that an unstick to the same step carries no Norn-Outcome, plus a non-holder-views case: a boundary for plan, then implement stuck and unstuck, still shows 'last boundary: plan'. Re-run `bun run golden -- --update`; the two unstick cases should lose the trailer.

findings.title: A CI read failure for a story held elsewhere fails the whole sync
findings.detail:
`ci: await ports.remote.pullRequestCi(pr.number)` sits inside the sync try. One failing `gh pr checks` (rate limit, a PR deleted between the two calls) throws, which sets sync.ok=false and skips `cache.synced_at`, for the sake of a view-only fact. findPullRequest behaves the same way, but CI is one extra call per story held elsewhere on every sync.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Catch per story and leave `ci` absent (the view prints 'not seen yet'), recording the error the way elsewhereError does.

findings.title: readRecordObjects misparses a `missing` reply from cat-file --batch
findings.detail:
The parser assumes every reply is `<sha> <type> <size>
<content>
`. For a missing object, git prints `<sha> missing
` with no content, so `size` is NaN. Every later entry is then read at a wrong offset and gets wrong text instead of an error. This happens with a shallow or partial clone, or a ref whose objects were pruned.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Check the header's type field. Report `missing` as a FileError for that path and advance only past the header line.

findings.title: commitFor's positional `fresh?: undefined` before `outcome`
findings.detail:
Every caller now passes `undefined` as the sixth argument to reach `outcome` (agent.ts:302, steps.ts:167, receipts.ts:213). The positional `fresh` and `outcome` slots are easy to swap.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Take an options object `{ fresh?, outcome? }`, or add a separate `boundaryCommitFor`.
